lessons: Filed ad-hoc and deliberately narrow. The 30d review was filed 2026-07-11 and 90d is not yet due; the only trigger is that forecast[2] carried a 'by 2026-07-30' window that has now elapsed — surfaced by the new eval check AS.

THE FINDING IS THE FORECAST, NOT THE COMPANY. HCG's FQ1 FY27 forecast was given a window ending 2026-07-30, but the company's own board meeting to approve those results is 2026-08-06 — a week AFTER the window closed. The forecast could never have been resolved inside its own window. That is a construction fault, and it is exactly the class of defect check AO (resolvability at authoring time) is meant to catch: the trigger named a settleable document but the WINDOW was not set to the date that document actually arrives. AO checks that a forecast CAN be settled; it does not check that its window contains the settling event.

Recorded 'still open' rather than 'not assessable'. The distinction matters for calibration: 'not assessable' means the evidence may never exist; here the evidence is scheduled, dated and six days away. Marking it not-assessable would quietly drop a resolvable forecast out of the scoring population.

The FQ1 print will be harder to score than the forecast assumed, for reasons dated after the decision and therefore NOT counted against the original process: HCG has since divested its non-core IVF business and listed rights-issue shares. Both distort the year-on-year revenue comparison the ~INR 7,340.9M consensus bar was built on. Whoever resolves this on 2026-08-06 must state which basis they are comparing.

Price fields are null in this review by choice, not by failure: this was a narrow, single-trigger ad-hoc filing and no fresh price was sourced. The 30d review (2026-07-11) carries the last price read on this record, and the 90d review is the right place for the next one. entry_price of INR 646.15 stands unchanged in the record (timestamped '2026-05, late-May 2026 pool snapshot').
Thesis status stays on-track: this is an Avoid, two months old, with nothing yet resolved for or against it. decision_quality is not assessable on the same ground.

memo_delta.summary: Nothing material has changed at the company since the memo, and that is the honest answer. The trigger for this filing is internal, not external: the FQ1 FY27 forecast carried a window ending 2026-07-30, but HCG's board does not meet to approve those results until 2026-08-06. The forecast could never have resolved inside its own window. Two post-decision corporate actions — the divestment of the non-core IVF business and the listing of rights-issue shares — will complicate the revenue comparison that forecast is measured against.
memo_delta.stage_one_comment: No change to the view on HCG. Nothing has been reported since our note - the company only meets on 6 August to approve its June quarter results, with the call the following day. The reason we are filing anything at all is a fault on our side rather than theirs: we set our first quarter revenue forecast to resolve by 30 July, a week before the company was ever going to publish the numbers, so it could not have been settled inside its own window. We have left it open and it should be resolved on 6 August against the roughly 7,341 million rupee consensus bar. One caution for whoever does that: the company has since sold its non-core fertility business and listed rights issue shares, so the year on year revenue comparison will not be like for like and the basis needs stating. The avoid stands and nothing in the last two months argues against it.
